accepted.question_text: For the hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem, where one must distinguish an Erdős-Rényi d-hypergraph G_d(N, 1/2) from a planted-clique alternative G_d(N, 1/2, κ) formed by choosing κ vertices uniformly at random and connecting every hyperedge whose vertices all lie in that planted set, what is the sharp threshold on the clique size κ at which polynomial-time singular-value-decomposition-based detection on a matricization or unfolding of the adjacency tensor succeeds, and is there some other polynomial-time algorithm that can solve HPC detection for κ below that SVD threshold?

accepted.question_text: Assuming the hypergraphic planted clique detection conjecture for fixed integer d ≥ 2, which states that when κ grows strictly slower than N no sequence of polynomial-time tests can distinguish the null model G_d(N, 1/2) from the planted-clique model G_d(N, 1/2, κ) with vanishing total error, can stronger evidence for this conjectured hardness be established for additional algorithmic frameworks beyond the Metropolis and low-degree polynomial methods already analyzed, specifically for classes such as statistical query, sum-of-squares, belief propagation, and approximate message passing?

accepted.question_text: At the regime κ = O(N^(1/2-τ)) for τ > 0, what is the precise average-case computational relationship between hypergraphic planted clique detection and ordinary planted clique detection? More specifically, since the paper states that HPC detection is no harder than PC detection because there is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from HPC to PC that preserves the planted clique size κ, can one also construct a randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC to HPC, thereby proving that the two detection problems are computationally equivalent in this threshold regime?
accepted.context_brief: Equivalence of HPC and PC hardness

evidence.quote:
Challenge 3 At the threshold level of κ “ OpN 1{2´τ q for τ ą 0, what is relationship between
HPC detection and PC detection in their computational hardness?

First, HPC detection is no harder than PC detection. Given the adjacency tensor A of
hypergraph G, by ﬁxing pd ´ 2q indices and varying the remaining two, we get an adjacency
matrix A from A which is a PC detection problem. So we can do a randomized polynomial-
time reduction from HPC detection to PC detection without changing the planted clique
size κ.

If reduction from PC to HPC could be proved, we would be able to arrive
at the conclusion that PC and HPC detection are equivalently hard and all hardness results
established in PC detection can be applied to HPC.
